description:
Per VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md and the CLAUDE.md rule that V&V documentation must carry BOTH methodology and measured results.

THE HONEST POSITION: no integrated nuclear-refinery plant exists, so the whole flowsheet cannot be validated end to end. Validation is therefore per block, plus conservation checks on the assembly. Say this plainly in the docs instead of implying plant-level validation.

PER-BLOCK TARGETS: distillation column against a published test problem from the open separations literature; flash and property packages against the existing dwsim-libs test suite and published phase-equilibrium data; reformer against published equilibrium composition data; heat exchanger against LMTD/NTU analytical cases.
ASSEMBLY-LEVEL CHECKS: mass and energy closure across the converged flowsheet to a stated tolerance, and a pinch check proving no heat flows up a temperature gradient.
HEAT SOURCE: inherits the HTR-10 V&V status, which is currently nothing. Until the pebble-bed closures are validated, every result carries an explicitly labelled unvalidated heat source.

Record measured numbers with uncertainty and the date taken. Never report a result that was not produced by running the check.
title: refinery: V&V plan — what each block is validated against, and what cannot be validated

description:
Found and diagnosed 2026-08-12 while implementing the six-equation solver (op-62vf). Recorded as a KNOWN LIMITATION with a measured boundary, not as a mystery.

SYMPTOM. TwoFluid1d marches a two-phase blowdown (saturated 7 MPa, alpha_g = 0.1, 1 mm bubbles, 24 cells, dt = 30 us) for the full 300 ms -- 10002 steps, p falls 7.0 MPa -> 0.494 MPa, alpha_g -> 0.993, |T_g - T_l| = 5.93 K, slip 0.279 m/s. The SAME transient started at alpha_g = 1e-4 refuses after 5-11 steps.

MECHANISM (diagnosed, not guessed). Each phase energy equation carries the reversible work term alpha_k dp/dt, i.e. dh_k = dp / rho_k per unit mass of that phase. In a depressurisation this cools the vapour along very nearly an isentrope. The only thing that heats it back toward T_sat(p) is interfacial heat transfer, whose volumetric coefficient scales as 6 alpha_d lambda Nu / d^2 -- proportional to interfacial area and hence to void fraction. At small alpha_g there is almost no area, the vapour cools faster than T_sat falls, and within a few steps it is more than MAX_METASTABLE_VAPOUR_SUBCOOLING (30 K) below saturation, where PhaseState::vapour_at refuses. The mirror case is a saturated start where flashing outruns the same area and the LIQUID leaves its 30 K superheat bound.

MEASURED (2026-08-12, release, 24 cells, dt = 30 us, ramped 87% break):
  57 K subcooled, alpha_g=1e-4, d=1 mm  : 11 steps, vapour past 30 K subcooling
  57 K subcooled, alpha_g=1e-4, d=0.1 mm: 10 steps, same
  57 K subcooled, alpha_g=1e-4, d=10 um :  5 steps, same
  saturated,      alpha_g=1e-4, d=1 mm  : 10 steps, liquid past 30 K superheat
  saturated,      alpha_g=1e-4, d=10 um : 11 steps, volume residual 1.23e-3 (see the separate bead)
  saturated,      alpha_g=0.1 , d=1 mm  : 10002 steps, full 300 ms, completed

NOT FIXED BY REFINEMENT. A smaller timestep does not help: the isentropic cooling per unit PRESSURE drop is a thermodynamic fact and the pressure drop is set by the transient, not by dt.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT, in rough order of honesty:
  1. A wall/bulk nucleation source and an interfacial-area-concentration transport equation, so alpha_d and d respond to the flow instead of being prescribed. This is the real answer and it is a substantial piece of work.
  2. Failing that, treating the vapour work term with an implicit coupling to the interfacial heat transfer, so the two are solved together rather than sequentially.
  3. NOT acceptable: widening MAX_METASTABLE_VAPOUR_SUBCOOLING. The property layer is refusing correctly; the state really is outside what IF97 Region 2 can be extrapolated to.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EDWARDS CASE (op-s1a0). Edwards-O'Brien starts 57 K SUBCOOLED, which is exactly the regime that refuses. A two-fluid Edwards case is therefore blocked on this, not merely unwritten. Whoever picks it up should read this bead first rather than tuning the initial void fraction until it runs.

RECORDED IN CODE: two_fluid_tests::six_equation_march_refuses_where_a_phase_cannot_shed_its_expansion_work pins the boundary and carries the measured table; DEFAULT_INITIAL_VOID_FRACTION documents the stand-in.
title: tampines TwoFluid1d: low-void starts refuse -- vapour cannot shed its expansion work without a nucleation / interfacial-area model

description:
Both app/mod.rs:133 and side_panel.rs:87 clone the entire FHRState every repaint, to read a handful of scalars. FHRState carries 15 Vec<f64> node-temperature vectors, so that is ~30 heap allocations plus memcpy per frame, ~1800/s at 60 fps.

Lock discipline is already correct (app/mod.rs:134 drops the guard immediately), so this is pure allocation waste, not contention.

Fix: clone once per frame and pass a reference, or copy out only the scalars each panel needs.

Measure before and after with the new GUI frame-time readout added 2026-08-12 (app/gui_frame_metrics.rs, displayed in the side panel). Do not assume this is the cause of perceived lag -- physics is only at 20% duty (TH loop <20000 us against a 100000 us budget) and the plot buffers are bounded, so the GUI is where the cost must be, but the split between our ui() body and egui tessellation/paint is not yet known.
title: fhr_sim_v2: GUI clones the whole FHRState twice per frame
